strengths: Core methodology (GP residual correction, kernel/feature comparison) independently reproduced on real AME data.
Qualitative claims (RMSE reduction, Matérn > RBF coverage, length-scale expansion, feature improvement) confirmed.
Dataset counts and selection criteria matched closely (AME2016 2271 vs 2272, AME2020 74 exact).
All tested numeric claims agree within expected limits given bare-model substitution.
Honest limitation: did not use the eight published mass models (DZ28, WS3, etc.), so absolute RMSE claims not directly tested.
No contradictions or refutations found; all qualitative claims survived.
Reproducibility artifacts and code are complete and transparent.
weaknesses: Absolute test-set RMSE (<150 keV on AME2020) not reproduced due to using a much weaker bare mass model (LDM vs DZ28/WS3).
GP-8D Matérn kernel overfit in sklearn, leading to zero training RMSE; paper uses GPy, so hyperparameter priors differ.
Coverage score reduced by inability to test claims requiring the eight published mass models.
Agreement score limited by lack of direct numeric comparison for the paper's best-performing models.
Did not pull the paper's GP predictions from Science Data Bank for cross-verification (deliberately, to preserve independence).
one_line_summary: Replication confirms the paper's methodology and qualitative claims using independent data and code, but cannot reproduce absolute RMSEs due to lack of the eight published mass models, yielding a robust PARTIAL verdict.
